subject: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Hi Alice —

Great to speak earlier today. As promised, here’s a short recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off the POC next week: 

Recap from today’s call:
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for Acme Health’s triage assistant use case (HIPAA-safe private deployment).
- Primary success criteria (proposal): 1) P95 latency < 400ms for 90% of production queries; 2) throughput meets sustained 120 RPS with 500 concurrent sessions; 3) generation quality parity with your existing model as measured on the shared eval set (we’ll use the 200-sample prompt set you mentioned).

Immediate requests we need from your team to finalize the trial plan:
1) Workload profile: average prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, peak RPS, expected concurrency, burst characteristics (duration and frequency).
2) Example traffic file (CSV is fine) and a redacted sample of 50 prompts for evaluation.
3) Confirmation of timeline: target kickoff week of Apr 19 and 4-week evaluation window.

Proposed owners and next steps:
- Redwood: Ben (owner) — commercial coordination; Dylan (SE) — technical setup and workload tuning; Marissa (CS) — onboarding and success metrics.
- Acme Health: Alice (POC lead), Tom (infra).

Attachments mentioned on call: we’ll send a POC evaluation plan template (poc-eval-plan.xlsx) and would appreciate your sample_traffic.csv.

If this looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for the kickoff and DLs for the accounts.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
Note: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a private deployment option for PHI/PII-sensitive data.

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Thanks Ben — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming we’re aligned on kickoff week of Apr 19. I attached a preliminary sample_traffic.csv with one week of anonymized traffic and a short note outlining our high-level SLA expectations.

Quick answers (high level) — I’ll follow up with Tom for exact numbers if you need more granularity:
- Avg prompt tokens: 45
- Avg completion tokens: 120
- Sustained baseline RPS: 80
- Target sustained RPS for POC: 120
- Peak burst RPS observed: 600 (typically lasts 30–90s during morning syncs, ~2–3x per day)
- Expected concurrency: ~400 sessions; spikes to ~900 during product launches.

We’ll also send the 50-sample eval prompts by end of day tomorrow. Please share the POC evaluation template and any other lift items for our infra team (Tom).

Attachments: sample_traffic.csv (anonymized), acme_requirements.docx

Best,
Alice Johnson
Product Ops Lead | Acme Health
alice.johnson@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Thanks Alice — that’s perfect and helpful.

I’ve drafted the POC evaluation plan and success criteria based on your numbers and the outcomes you care about. High level:
- Timeline: Kickoff Apr 19, week 1 integration & smoke tests, week 2 steady-state load tests & evals, week 3 fine-tuning and regression checks, week 4 final comparison and handoff.
- Success criteria:
  * Performance: P50 < 120ms, P95 < 400ms under sustained 120 RPS and 500 concurrent sessions.
  * Resilience: tolerate bursts to 600–900 RPS for short durations without errors (>99% success).
  * Accuracy: model meets or exceeds baseline aggregated F1/ROUGE on your 200-sample eval suite (we’ll run blind).
  * Cost target: less than $X per 1M tokens (we’ll provide two configuration options: low-latency and cost-optimized).
- Ownership: Redwood will provision a private trial environment (dedicated pool) and handle rollout/transitions. Marissa will track success metrics and weekly checkpoints; Ben will own commercial terms.

Dylan — can you review the technical checklist in the attached poc-eval-plan.xlsx and call out any missing inputs we need from Tom before kickoff?

I’ll send the kickoff invite once we have a confirmed time from Tom.

Thanks — looking forward.
Ben

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Thanks — quick technical follow-up / checklist before the kickoff so we can size the Dedicated pool correctly: 

1) Traffic profile clarifications (please confirm):
   - Sustained RPS for baseline tests: 120 RPS (Alice confirmed).
   - Peak bursts: 600 RPS for 30–90s, occasional spikes to 900 RPS (we should know frequency).
   - Concurrency: 400 typical, up to 900.
2) Token distribution:
   - Avg prompt tokens: 45
   - Avg completion tokens: 120
   - Tail behavior: what % of requests exceed 512 tokens combined? (we need % of >512 and >1024).
3) Latency SLOs: P95 < 400ms — confirm whether that’s for end-to-end (app -> Redwood) or inference-only (token gen).
4) Auth / data handling:
   - Will requests include PHI? (Alice previously said HIPAA — confirm scope)
   - Retention: how long should logs/inputs be kept? (default: 30 days unless you need longer)
5) TLS and network egress constraints for the private deployment (Tom).

Sizing note: with 120 RPS sustained and avg generation of 120 tokens, we recommend starting with a 4-GPU dedicated pool (A6000-equivalent) with auto-burst to 8 GPUs for short peaks; for cost-optimized tests we can switch to an int8 quantized variant to drop token cost ~2.5x (tradeoff ~small quality delta).

I attached the poc-eval-plan.xlsx (technical checklist & runbook) with the actions we’ll take each week. Tom — can you confirm the >512 token % and your security/KMS requirements so we can finalize provisioning?

- Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial planning - workload intake & success criteria

Dylan / Ben — thanks for the checklist. Tom and I pulled the traffic for the last 30 days and updated the CSV (attached). Final answers from infra: 
- % requests >512 tokens combined: ~3%
- % requests >1024 tokens combined: ~0.4%
- Burst frequency: ~3 times/day, 30–90s; 1–2 times/month for business-critical launches hitting 800–900 RPS for 3–5 minutes.
- PHI scope: yes — some user-provided notes can include PHI, so we’ll need private deployment and KMS/HSM integration.
- Log retention: 90 days internal retention (we’ll discuss redaction options).
- Network: VPC peering preferred; egress restrictions will be provided to your infra contact.

We reviewed your recommended sizing and it sounds reasonable. Please include the int8 quantized config as the cost-optimized option and the low-latency config for the performance tests.

Next steps:
- Ben: send commercial quote for the 4-week POC + optional burst capacity and SOC2 evidence.
- Dylan / Marissa: schedule a 1-hour kickoff on Mon Apr 19 for integration and KMS/setup.
- Alice / Tom: we’ll share the eval prompts and confirm preferred kickoff time by EOD today.

Attachments: updated_sample_traffic.csv (replaced), acme_requirements.docx

Appreciate the responsiveness — excited to get started.

Best,
Alice
